prompt:
Our app lets signed-in users keep personal files like receipts and bank
statements. These files are private — a user must only ever be able to upload
and download their own. The app uploads each file under a path that starts
with the owner's user id, e.g. `<user_id>/receipt-march.pdf`.

Set up a `user-files` bucket on our project and lock it down that way.

Users also sometimes share one of their files with someone else through a
temporary link that expires. Include the supabase-js code the app should use
for that.

checks.name: documented live deployment and verification steps
checks.judgeNotes: README includes a Supabase Secret API key step and basic verification via Prometheus targets, but it does not require placing the matching secret file or restarting/reloading the Compose stack. The provided Prometheus config also hardcodes `sb_secret_test` and `testproj`, while README describes env vars that are not actually used, causing a mismatched secret setup.

prompt:
Last week support removed a user through our app's delete-account flow — the
app calls the `delete_account` function over RPC as the signed-in user. This
morning that same person was back: still signed in, reading and saving their
data like nothing happened.

Figure out why the account still works, fix the flow so a deleted account
loses access, and tell me whether there is any window where they could still
get in after the fix.

One more thing while you're at it: we're migrating off the legacy
anon/service_role API keys to the new publishable and secret keys, and the
team isn't sure which one belongs in the frontend and what each means for
RLS. Give us a quick rundown.

prompt:
Our dispatch dashboard shows incoming orders as they happen. The courier
location feed on the same page updates live without problems, but new orders
only show up after a page refresh.

The dashboard uses supabase-js to subscribe to INSERT events on the `orders`
table through postgres_changes, the same way it subscribes to courier
locations. The channel's status callback logs SUBSCRIBED and there are no
errors in the browser console.

Figure out why no order events ever arrive and fix it.

checks.name: identified image-transform and the recurring 503 pattern
checks.judgeNotes: The assistant identified image-transform as affected and described repeated/periodic 503s throughout the morning of 2026-04-28. It did not enumerate all 8 gateway failures or exact 07:00Z-12:00Z span, but it recognized the recurring morning pattern and named the function.

checks.name: attributed recurring 503s to gateway/platform layer, not function code
checks.judgeNotes: The assistant mentions gateway 503s, but primarily attributes the issue to function runtime/dependency/upstream service or flaky deployment and recommends redeploying the functions. It does not clearly conclude that the recurring image-transform 503s originate at the gateway/platform layer in front of the function, nor ground that attribution in observations like absence of invocation/runtime rows, unchanged deployment_id, or distinction from the avatar-upload 500.

checks.name: recommended a concrete next step
checks.judgeNotes: The assistant recommended concrete next steps: inspect Edge Function runtime logs around 503 timestamps, check upstream/package outages, redeploy affected functions, add explicit error logging, and verify upstream timeouts/rate limits.
